outcome: Uterine Fibroid Symptom and health-related Quality of Life (UFS-QoL) symptoms score
Complications (groin haematomatas, endometritis, urinary tract infections)
cohort: 117 women with magnetic resonance imaging features of symptomatic adenomyosis (junctional zone thickness >= 12 mm) who had unsuccessful conservative management for adenomyosis-related heavy menstrual bleeding and dysmenorrhoea and underwent uterine artery embolisation.
finding: Uterine artery embolisation (UAE) was found to be an effective uterine-sparing option for women with symptomatic adenomyosis who had unsuccessful conservative treatments, achieving high rates of clinical success, HMB control, and dysmenorrhoea relief with no major complications.
